$comment: The written exceptions to the Git Crafter CI standard (tools/ci_standard.py, templates/ci/README.md) for the three reusable workflows other repositories call. A caller's run, not this repository's, holds each one's triggers and concurrency; each exception names its reason.

gitleaks.yml/gitleaks.why: A reusable workflow runs on the caller's kind of repository: the label is computed from the caller's visibility, so one fixed hosted label cannot serve a public and a private caller. A public caller runs on the light hosted label.

gitleaks.yml.why: A reusable workflow cannot own its caller's concurrency group, and the caller's workflow sets it. The scan is short, and it reads the whole history on every run, so a cancelled older run would only hide a finding.

gemini-review.yml/review.why: runner: computed from the caller's visibility, as gitleaks.yml. cache: the job installs one command-line tool globally at a pinned version, and the repository holds no npm lockfile or package.json, so setup-node has nothing to key a cache on.

gemini-review.yml/gate.why: Computed from the caller's visibility, as gitleaks.yml: the date gate runs on the same kind of runner as the review it guards.

dependabot-automerge.yml/automerge.why: Computed from the caller's visibility, as gitleaks.yml: a public caller runs on a standard hosted label.

dependabot-automerge.yml.why: A reusable workflow cannot own its caller's concurrency group. The job only turns on auto-merge and checks first whether it is already on, so a repeat run changes nothing.
